summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:finishing-a-development-branch, ran the full suite (about 12 minutes, 7 tests including the corpus replay) as a background job, and kept its turn open the whole time. It reported that the suite passed, showed the options, and after I answered "1" it fast-forward merged feature/strip-accents into main and deleted the branch. It stopped only once, to show the integration options. The test files were not changed.
reasoning: Each criterion is backed by the session log, the suite log, or git/md5 checks. The agent kept its turn open with a spinner for the whole 12-minute suite. It stopped before the merge only once, to ask which option to take, and then merged successfully.

observations.description: The final pre-merge message asked two questions at once: whether the base is main, and which option to pick. One reply had to cover both. The agent took '1' (Merge back to main locally) as covering both.
The options list showed only 3 choices (merge, PR, keep). There was no 'discard' option, although the story expects discard to be one of the choices.

Claude Code startup dialogs: the folder trust prompt and the bypass-permissions prompt both default to 'No, exit'. A 'Newer Opus model available' prompt also appeared, saying the pinned model was Opus 5, even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. I chose No, and the header then showed 'Opus 5.5'.
Mid-run, the status line showed 'Update installed · Restart to update'. This is harmless here.
The test run left untracked slugkit/__pycache__ and tests/__pycache__. The agent pointed this out and suggested adding a .gitignore.
The suite output was written under the codex-review cache directory (home/.cache/hyperpowers/codex-review/...), which is an odd place for a finishing-branch test log.

criteria.evidence: suite.log ends with 'corpus 35/35 ... ok', 'Ran 7 tests in 700.248s', 'OK'. Agent said: 'The full suite passed: 7 tests, including the corpus replay, in about 11.7 minutes (700s).'
